scenes.visual: Title card 'Trend and Chance' over a faint fan of blue runs above a red-orange dashed floor. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: thin BLUE lines = population runs, plotted as log numbers (y) against years (x); RED-ORANGE dashed line = the floor; GOLD arrow = the trend; grey jitter band = the swings. Film 2 adds TEAL = Florida ancestry, PURPLE = Texas ancestry, TEAL-PURPLE stripes = admixed. Cream background, 16:9. Numbers appear only as on-screen text. Runs and fractions are computed from a random walk on log numbers (trend and swings as labelled, floor 10 animals) and labelled 'computed'; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Which population is in more danger? One shrinks a little on average each year. The other grows a little, but its numbers swing wildly. Both start with fifty animals.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left: a smooth blue run sliding gently downward, label 'shrinks a little, small swings (trend below zero)'. Right: a jagged blue run climbing slowly while jumping up and down, label 'grows a little, wild swings (trend above zero)'. Both start at a tag 'start: 50'. A question mark between them. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Which population is in more danger? One shrinks a little on average each year. The other grows a little, but its numbers swing wildly. Both start with fifty animals.

scenes.tts: Put one population on a chart. Each blue line is one possible run of its numbers. The red dashed line is the floor, a number too low to recover from.
scenes.visual: One blue run draws itself left to right across 100 years on a log-numbers axis. A red-orange dashed line slides in near the bottom, label 'floor'. Axis labels 'years' and 'numbers (log scale)'.
scenes.narration: Put one population on a chart. Each blue line is one possible run of its numbers. The red dashed line is the floor, a number too low to recover from.

scenes.tts: Two things move the line. The gold arrow is the trend, the average yearly change on a log scale. Around it the line jitters up and down. Those are the swings, the good years and bad.
scenes.visual: A gold arrow lays itself along the run's overall slope, label 'trend: average yearly change in log numbers'. A grey band around the arrow pulses, label 'swings'. The blue run keeps jittering inside the band.
scenes.narration: Two things move the line. The gold arrow is the trend, the average yearly change on a log scale. Around it the line jitters up and down. Those are the swings, the good years and bad.

scenes.tts: Now run the same population two hundred times. The runs fan out. Some touch the floor. The fraction that touches it is the risk.
scenes.visual: Computed: 200 blue runs spray out from the same start, fanning wider with time. Each run that touches the floor turns red-orange and stops. A counter at right ticks up: 'touched the floor: x of 200', converting to a percentage.
scenes.narration: Now run the same population two hundred times. The runs fan out. Some touch the floor. The fraction that touches it is the risk.

scenes.tts: That is the idea behind a population viability analysis. A real one runs a fuller model many times, and counts the runs that fall.
scenes.caption: That is the idea behind a population viability analysis (PVA). A real one runs a fuller model many times, and counts the runs that fall.
scenes.visual: The counter becomes a label card 'population viability analysis (PVA): the fraction of runs that reach the floor within a chosen time'. Small tag under it: 'real PVAs add ages, crowding, catastrophes'. The fan stays behind it.
scenes.narration: That is the idea behind a population viability analysis (PVA). A real one runs a fuller model many times, and counts the runs that fall.

scenes.tts: Turn two dials, one at a time. Widen the swings, and more runs touch the floor. Raise the start, and fewer runs do.
scenes.visual: Two dial icons, 'swings' and 'start'. Turning 'swings' up: the computed fan widens and more runs turn red-orange; counter rises. Turning 'start' up: the whole fan lifts away from the floor; counter falls.
scenes.narration: Turn two dials, one at a time. Widen the swings, and more runs touch the floor. Raise the start, and fewer runs do.

scenes.tts: Now tilt the gold arrow down, so the population shrinks on average. Will starting with ten times as many animals save it?
scenes.visual: The third dial, 'trend', turns: the gold arrow tilts downward. Two fans side by side: 'start 50' and 'start 500', both with the arrow tilted down (label 'trend below zero').
scenes.narration: Now tilt the gold arrow down, so the population shrinks on average. Will starting with ten times as many animals save it?

scenes.visual: Hold both fans at year 0. Caption 'Predict: does a tenfold bigger start save a shrinking population?' with a 5-second countdown.

scenes.tts: Over one century, the bigger start helps a lot. Far fewer runs touch the floor. But keep the clock running. Over a thousand years, nearly every run reaches it.
scenes.visual: Computed, trend -0.02 per year, swings 0.2: at 100 years the counters read 'start 50: about 73% touched the floor' and 'start 500: about 23%'. The time axis stretches to 1,000 years and both counters climb to 'nearly 100%'.
scenes.narration: Over one century, the bigger start helps a lot. Far fewer runs touch the floor. But keep the clock running. Over a thousand years, nearly every run reaches it.

scenes.tts: The bigger population bought time, not safety. With the arrow pointing down, every start reaches the floor in the end. How soon depends on the trend, the start and the swings together. Tilt it up to plus point oh two, and most runs stay clear.
scenes.visual: Banner 'size buys time'. Small tag 'how soon: trend, start and swings together'. Then the gold arrow tilts upward: computed, trend +0.02 per year, swings 0.2, start 50; the fan rises and most runs stay clear of the floor, counter 'about 18% touched the floor in 1,000 years', label 'trend +0.02: most runs stay clear'.
scenes.narration: The bigger population bought time, not safety. With the arrow pointing down, every start reaches the floor in the end. How soon depends on the trend, the start and the swings together. Tilt it up to plus point oh two, and most runs stay clear.

scenes.tts: With few animals, one unlucky litter can decide the outcome. So chance in single births and deaths weighs most near the floor.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the bottom of the chart near the floor. Small animal icons appear on one run, a few blinking out, label 'few animals: chance in single births and deaths'. Small footnote tag: 'schematic; the computed runs keep the swings steady'. No widening band.
scenes.narration: With few animals, one unlucky litter can decide the outcome. So chance in single births and deaths weighs most near the floor.

scenes.tts: Genes can tilt the arrow too. Fewer animals means more mating among relatives. Inbreeding can lower survival and fertility, so the trend tilts down and numbers fall further. This loop is called the extinction vortex.
scenes.visual: A circular loop of four labelled boxes with arrows: 'fewer animals' to 'more inbreeding' to 'lower survival and fertility' to 'trend tilts down' and back to 'fewer animals'. The gold arrow on the chart tilts further down each time the loop turns. Label 'extinction vortex'. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Genes can tilt the arrow too. Fewer animals means more mating among relatives. Inbreeding can lower survival and fertility, so the trend tilts down and numbers fall further. This loop is called the extinction vortex.

scenes.tts: Back to the two populations. The shrinking one will reach the floor in time, however big it starts. The growing one can escape. Its risk still depends on trend, size and swings together.
scenes.visual: Return to the opening split screen, now as computed fans over 1,000 years. Left fan (trend below zero) all runs end red-orange, tag 'fix the trend, add numbers'. Right fan (trend above zero, wide swings) many runs survive, tag 'trend, numbers and swings together'.
scenes.narration: Back to the two populations. The shrinking one will reach the floor in time, however big it starts. The growing one can escape. Its risk still depends on trend, size and swings together.

scenes.tts: This gives managers a target, for one population in one habitat. A minimum viable population is the smallest start that keeps the risk below a chosen level, over a chosen time.
scenes.caption: This gives managers a target, for one population in one habitat. A minimum viable population (MVP) is the smallest start that keeps the risk below a chosen level, over a chosen time.
scenes.visual: The 'start' dial slides up until the counter drops below a dashed target line labelled 'chosen risk, chosen time'. The start value at that point is tagged 'minimum viable population (MVP)'.
scenes.narration: This gives managers a target, for one population in one habitat. A minimum viable population (MVP) is the smallest start that keeps the risk below a chosen level, over a chosen time.

scenes.tts: So conservation starts by removing the cause of decline. Alongside it, numbers, connections and genes can lift the trend or cut the risk. But in this model, without a trend above zero, size only buys time.
scenes.visual: Two numbered cards build: '1. Find and remove the cause of decline' (gold arrow swings upward) and '2. Alongside: numbers, connections, genes, which can lift the trend or cut the risk' (the arrow lifts a little more, the fan rises). Footnote: 'In this model, without a trend above zero, size only buys time.'
scenes.narration: So conservation starts by removing the cause of decline. Alongside it, numbers, connections and genes can lift the trend or cut the risk. But in this model, without a trend above zero, size only buys time.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Take-home line: 'In this model, without a trend above zero, size only buys time.'
